newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals firmer, could hold gains.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals firmer, could hold gains.

text.p: Precious metals on Wednesday retained the gains made during a frantic fund-led late rally on Tuesday that left dealers and analysts wary of predicting what happens next.
Late Tuesday , gold rose from an early 3-3/4-year low fix of $336.90 per ounce to around $347, silver gained about 35 cents from $4.82 and platinum surged $14.00 to $369.00.
"That was too much of a shock yesterday to give up the gains straight away. We are looking to buy on dips but be prepared to sell gold at over $345," one senior dealer said.
Gold fixed at $343.00 in London on Wednesday up from $337.70 on Tuesday afternoon and a close of $340.90/$341.40.
"Yesterday's sharp rally suggests we have seen the lows for now," said technical analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge.
Another analyst said one of the issues that convinced the hedge funds to cover short gold positions and even add fresh metal to the portfolio was the increasing reluctance of the market to go lower.
"The downside seemed to be limited to $340-$336 so the funds bought back. It was a clever exit strategy to lock in profits," he said on the basis of anonymity.
Whether or not the funds stay that way is another matter.
"That's the decision for this week," said bullion markets analyst Andy Smith at Union Bank of Switzerland. "There is quite a lot of short covering mileage left in the market," he added.
Smith also noted that gold had some way to go to catch up with the other metals against some technical measures.
Silver and palladium after their bounces yeterday had both broken their 200-day moving averages at $5.04 and $124.00 respectively and platinum was through its 50-day of $362.00.
"But gold is no where near even its 50-day moving average of $359. It is clearly the laggard," Smith said.
Platinum fixed at its highest level since January 2 at $368.50 to establish a $25.50 premium over gold.
"It had been dragged down by gold unnecessarily. Now it is at a sensible premium," a platinum dealer said.

But the market is being held up by delays to crucial Russia platinum and palladium exports. A Russian decision to start delayed supply talks with Japanese and other key importers could knock prices back severely.
Palladium was at $141.00/$142.00 after a highest fix ($141.00) since March 27, 1996 and silver was 23 cents up at $5.12/$5.15. -Brian Spoors London Newsroom +44 171 542 8058
